mainTopic: Which invalidly pinched or slaughtered bird offerings make one impure in the throat like a נבלה, and which disqualified offerings come down from the מזבח
overview: The גמרא first shows that the משנה's two general clauses each add their own case (שחיטת קדשים בפנים and מליקת חולין בחוץ), so the משנה says nothing about מליקת זר. A ברייתא then supports רבי יוחנן: a bird pinched by a זר does not make one impure in the throat. רבי יצחק heard that one of קמיצת זר and מליקת זר comes down from the מזבח and one does not, and חזקיה reasons that the קמיצה comes down. The גמרא defends this split: a מנחה on a בָּמָה had no קידוש in a כלי שרת, so the בָּמָה cannot serve as a model for a Temple מנחה. Two ברייתות then use the word 'טריפה' to decide which badly killed birds make clothing טמא in the throat. The test for pinching is whether the act permits something forbidden. The test for slaughter is whether the bird is the same inside and outside the עזרה. רבא adds that slaughter outside, which brings כרת, keeps the bird from being a נבלה. רב שימי בר אשי limits the comparison to two improper acts, and a challenge from a ברייתא about a יוצא is answered with the פסוק 'זאת תורת העולה'. Finally a new משנה opens: רבי מאיר rules that a properly pinched bird found to be a טריפה does not make one impure in the throat.

steps.title: If the first clause adds something, what does the second clause add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the inference from the משנה. If one clause must 'add' a case, the matching clause must also add one, and the inference does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, the clause 'whose disqualification did not happen in the holy place' comes to add what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an attempted inference from the משנה by turning the same logic onto the משנה's other clause. It shows that this style of reading creates a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attempted inference said an extra clause in the משנה must come to add a case like מליקת זר. The גמרא replies that the parallel clause, about disqualifications not in the קודש, would also need its own added case. By the same pattern, that added case would have to be מליקת זר. So the inference proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the other side's logic back on them
To include what? What extra case does this phrase add?
Its disqualification happened in the holy place, meaning the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new question about the law. It is a tool that knocks down how the משנה was being read, so the earlier inference loses its force.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
'whose disqualification did not happen in the holy place'
comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an inference made just before this section, which read the משנה's clause as including מליקת זר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the method of reading the משנה's general clause as a source for מליקת זר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The parallel clause would then also need an added case, and the same logic would point it at מליקת זר, which leads to a contradiction

steps.title: Each clause adds a different case
steps.stepSummary: The first clause adds slaughter of sacred birds inside. The second clause adds pinching of non-sacred birds outside. Neither clause is about מליקת זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the first clause adds slaughtering sacred birds inside, and the second clause adds pinching non-sacred birds outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each clause of the משנה really adds. This removes any proof about מליקת זר from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטת קדשים בפנים is a wrong method used inside the עזרה. It does not make the bird a נבלה, which fits the first clause. מליקת חולין בחוץ is pinching a plain bird outside. That is not a real שחיטה, so the bird is a נבלה, which fits the second clause. Since both clauses now have their own cases, the משנה tells us nothing about מליקת זר.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching the neck of a bird offering with the כהן's thumbnail

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's two general clauses add שחיטת קדשים בפנים (not impure) and מליקת חולין בחוץ (impure). They do not decide מליקת זר.

phrases.english: Rather, the first clause
comes to include slaughtering sacred birds inside,
the last clause
comes to include pinching non-sacred birds outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by giving each clause its own added case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning what each clause comes to include
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's clauses might hint at the law of מליקת זר
steps.terutzMaskana: The clauses cover שחיטת קדשים בפנים and מליקת חולין בחוץ, so the משנה is silent about מליקת זר

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a bird pinched by a זר or by a disqualified כהן, or one that is פיגול, נותר, or טמא, does not make one impure in the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches like רבי יוחנן: If a non-כהן pinched it, or a disqualified person pinched it, or it is פיגול, נותר, or טמא, these do not make one impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that clearly matches רבי יוחנן's ruling about מליקת זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said מליקת זר does not make the bird a נבלה for impurity in the throat. The ברייתא lists מלקה זר right at the start, together with other offerings ruined only inside the קודש. All of them are not impure in the throat, which confirms רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him
An offering made with intent to eat it past its allowed time
Meat left over past its allowed time
The throat, where a bird נבלה makes the person swallowing it impure

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives clear outside support to רבי יוחנן. A bird pinched by a זר is treated like other offerings ruined in the קודש, not like a נבלה.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan:
if a non-priest pinched it,
if a disqualified priest pinched it,
the piggul, the notar, and the impure one,
do not make one impure in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה turned out to be no proof either way, a ברייתא is brought that directly supports רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that מליקת זר does not make one impure in the throat
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists מלקה זר among cases that are not impure in the throat

steps.title: רבי יצחק heard two rulings but forgot which is which
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק heard about קמיצת זר and מליקת זר. One of them comes down from the מזבח and one does not, but he does not remember which.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: I heard two rulings, one about a non-כהן taking the handful and one about a non-כהן pinching. One comes down and one does not come down, and I do not know which is which.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק reports a tradition he received only in part. He also sets up the question that חזקיה answers next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are offerings ruined by a זר doing the service. Normally some disqualified offerings that already went up on the מזבח stay there and are not taken down. רבי יצחק knows that one of these two cases stays up and the other is brought down, but he lost track of which is which.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard, as a received tradition
Taking a handful from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
It shall come down from the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
I heard two rulings:
one about a non-priest removing the handful,
and one about a non-priest pinching;
one shall come down, and one shall not come down;
phrases.notes: He means come down from the מזבח after it was already brought up there.

phrases.english: and I do not know which is which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from impurity in the throat to a related question: whether a disqualified offering that went up on the מזבח comes down
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of קמיצת זר and מליקת זר, one comes down from the מזבח and one does not, but the tradition does not say which

steps.title: חזקיה: the handful comes down, the pinched bird stays
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה reasons that קמיצת זר comes down from the מזבח and מליקת זר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: It makes sense that the handful comes down and the pinched bird does not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers רבי יצחק's doubt using logic, not a received tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק could not match the rulings to the cases, so חזקיה matches them by reasoning. He says the קמיצה done by a זר is taken down, while the bird pinched by a זר stays on the מזבח. Note that this is a 'מסתברא', a reasoned view, not a tradition he heard.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; a conclusion based on logic

steps.whatToRemember: According to חזקיה, קמיצת זר comes down from the מזבח and מליקת זר does not.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said: It stands to reason:
the handful shall come down,
the pinched bird shall not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the doubt רבי יצחק raised in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of קמיצת זר and מליקת זר comes down from the מזבח
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קמיצת זר comes down; מליקת זר does not

steps.title: What makes pinching different from removing a handful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why מליקה by a זר should be treated differently. If the reason is that it is valid on a בָּמָה, then קמיצה is also valid on a בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about pinching? Is it that it is valid on a private altar? Removing a handful is also valid on a private altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חזקיה's split between מליקת זר and קמיצת זר. It suggests a possible reason for the difference and immediately shows that the reason fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A possible reason for treating מליקה differently is that on a בָּמָה anyone, even a זר, could do the עבודה. But the same is true of קמיצה. So this reason cannot explain why the two cases come out differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching the back of a bird's neck to kill it as an offering
Removing a handful of flour from a מנחה
A private altar, used at times when that was allowed, where non-כהנים could serve

phrases.english: What is different about pinching?
phrases.notes: He means pinching done by a זר, from חזקיה's ruling just before.

phrases.english: That it is valid on a private altar?
Removing a handful is also valid on a private altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind חזקיה's ruling in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's distinction between מליקת זר and קמיצת זר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The suggested reason, that the act is valid on a בָּמָה, applies equally to both, so it cannot explain why they differ.

steps.title: If there was no meal offering on a private altar, there were no birds either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expects the answer that no מנחה was brought on a בָּמָה. It rejects that answer, because birds were not brought there either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say there was no meal offering on a private altar, then there were no birds on a private altar either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible defense of the difference. Someone might say קמיצה never happened on a בָּמָה, but the same would be true of birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense tries to make קמיצה different by saying מנחות were never brought on a בָּמָה. The גמרא answers that in that view birds were not brought there either. So מליקה and קמיצה are still in the same position.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא expects an answer and responds to it)
A meal offering made of flour

phrases.english: And if you will say there is no meal offering on a private altar,
There are no birds on a private altar either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects an expected answer to the challenge in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that קמיצה differs because no מנחה was brought on a בָּמָה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same reasoning removes birds from the בָּמָה too, so the two cases are still alike.

steps.title: רב ששת: meal offerings and birds go together on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת teaches that whoever allows a מנחה on a בָּמָה also allows birds, and whoever does not allow a מנחה does not allow birds. The reason is that the פסוק mentions only 'זבחים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ששת said: according to the one who says there was a meal offering on a private altar, there were birds on a private altar. According to the one who says there was no meal offering, there were no birds. What is the reason? 'Slaughtered offerings', and not meal offerings; 'slaughtered offerings', and not birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב ששת to prove the point of Step 7: מנחות and birds always go together when it comes to a בָּמָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת links the two cases. The view that excludes מנחות learns it from the word 'זבחים', and that same word also excludes birds. So you cannot remove מנחות from the בָּמָה and keep birds there.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: As רב ששת said:
According to the one who says there is a meal offering on a private altar,
There are birds on a private altar.
According to the one who says there is no meal offering,
There are no birds.
What is the reason?
'Slaughtered offerings', and not meal offerings,
'Slaughtered offerings', and not birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 7
steps.raayaObject: That birds and מנחות are treated the same regarding a בָּמָה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ששת, based on the word 'זבחים' in the פסוק

steps.title: The real difference: no sanctifying in a service vessel on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: a מנחה on a בָּמָה had no קידוש in a כלי שרת. So a מנחה on a בָּמָה cannot be compared to a מנחה in the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: there is no sanctifying in a service vessel for a meal offering on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier approach and gives a new reason why קמיצה cannot be compared to the בָּמָה the way מליקה can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both קמיצה and מליקה by a זר were valid on a בָּמָה. But a מנחה on a בָּמָה was missing קידוש in a כלי שרת, which the Temple always requires. So the בָּמָה is not a fair model for a Temple מנחה, while it can still serve as a model for birds.

keyTerms.meaning: A service vessel used in the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: The בָּמָה can serve as a model for מליקה by a זר, but not for קמיצה. A מנחה on a בָּמָה had no קידוש in a כלי שרת, so it is too different from a Temple מנחה.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
There is no sanctifying in a service vessel
phrases.notes: In the Temple, the handful must be put into a holy vessel. That step did not exist on a בָּמָה.

phrases.english: For a meal offering on a private altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reasoning of Steps 6 through 8 with a new answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the difference is that only מליקה by a זר is valid on a בָּמָה, or that no מנחה was brought there.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מנחה on a בָּמָה lacked קידוש in a כלי שרת, so it cannot be compared to the Temple. That is why קמיצת זר is not treated the same way as מליקת זר.

steps.title: A ברייתא asks whether an invalid pinching inside makes clothing impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a bird pinched with the left hand or at night. Then it brings a ברייתא: you might think such a bird makes clothing טמא in the throat, so the פסוק says 'נבלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he pinched with the left hand or at night, etc.' The רבנן taught: You might think that a pinching done inside the עזרה makes clothing טמא while the bird is in the throat. So the פסוק says: 'נבלה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that learns from the word 'נבלה' that an invalid pinching inside the עזרה does not make clothing טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird pinched with the left hand or at night was pinched in the wrong way, but it was still pinched inside the עזרה. The ברייתא asks whether it counts as a regular dead bird that makes the eater's clothing טמא. Its first answer rests on the word 'נבלה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing a bird קרבן by pinching the back of its neck with the כהן's fingernail
The throat, while the food is being swallowed
An animal or bird that died without a valid שחיטה

phrases.english: If he pinched with the left hand or at night, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
You might think that a pinching done inside
phrases.notes: He means a pinching that is invalid, like the left-hand or nighttime cases, even though it was done inside.

phrases.english: makes clothing impure while it is in the throat?
So the verse says: 'a carcass'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא מְלִיקָה שֶׁהִיא לִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה. It does not continue the בָּמָה discussion in Steps 5-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An invalid מליקה done inside the עזרה does not make clothing טמא in the throat. The first source given is the word 'נבלה'.

steps.title: But this bird is also a נבלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a bird pinched invalidly is also a נבלה, so the word 'נבלה' cannot be the source that leaves it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this one is also a נבלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the source the ברייתא just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird pinched with the left hand or at night is not a valid קרבן, so it should count as a נבלה. If so, the word 'נבלה' would include it, not leave it out. A different source is needed.

phrases.english: But this one is also a carcass!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning from the word 'נבלה' that an invalid pinching inside does not make clothing טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The invalidly pinched bird is itself a נבלה. So the word 'נבלה' points the opposite way.

steps.title: The source is the word טריפה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is read another way: the source is the word 'טריפה'. Just as a טריפה does not permit anything forbidden, only a death that does not permit anything forbidden makes clothing טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק says 'טריפה'. Just as a טריפה does not permit anything forbidden, so too anything that does not permit something forbidden is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source: the word 'טריפה' in the same פסוק. It sets up a rule that the next steps will apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule compares to a טריפה, which never makes anything forbidden become permitted. So the טומאה in the throat applies only to a death that does not permit anything forbidden. The question is no longer 'is it a נבלה?' but 'does this killing permit anything?'

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal injury

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says: 'a tereifa';

phrases.aramaic: מָה טְרֵיפָה – שֶׁאֵין מַתֶּרֶת אֶת הָאִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: just as a tereifa does not permit anything forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל – שֶׁאֵין מַתֶּרֶת אֶת הָאִיסּוּר.
phrases.english: so too anything that does not permit anything forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 11 by replacing the source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: the word 'טריפה' instead of 'נבלה'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'נבלה' leaves out the invalid pinching inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'טריפה' teaches the rule: only a killing that does not permit anything forbidden makes clothing טמא in the throat.

steps.title: An invalid pinching inside is left out
steps.stepSummary: Using the rule, an invalid pinching inside the עזרה is left out. It does permit something forbidden, so it does not make clothing טמא in the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: This leaves out a pinching done inside. Since it permits something forbidden, it does not make clothing טמא while in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the 'טריפה' rule to our משנה's case and leaves it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pinching inside, even an invalid one, does make something forbidden become permitted. So it is not like a טריפה. That is why the משנה says a bird pinched with the left hand or at night does not make clothing טמא.

phrases.english: This leaves out a pinching done inside,
phrases.notes: Some versions have יצא, in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is יָצָאת. Both mean 'is left out'.

phrases.english: since it permits something forbidden,
it does not make clothing impure while in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from Step 12 to the משנה's case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An invalid pinching inside the עזרה permits something forbidden. So it does not make clothing טמא in the throat.

steps.title: Pinching קדשים outside or חולין anywhere is included
steps.stepSummary: The rule includes pinching קדשים outside the עזרה, and pinching חולין inside or outside. These permit nothing forbidden, so they do make clothing טמא in the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes one who pinches (sign: קץ חפץ) קדשים outside, and one who pinches חולין inside or outside. Since these do not permit anything forbidden, they make clothing טמא in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by listing the cases the 'טריפה' rule includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים pinched outside can never be offered. חולין can never be offered, wherever they are pinched. Nothing becomes permitted in these cases, so they are just like a טריפה and make clothing טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to help remember a list

steps.whatToRemember: The test is not 'is it a נבלה?' but 'does this killing permit anything forbidden?' An invalid pinching inside permits something, so it does not make clothing טמא. Pinching קדשים outside, or חולין anywhere, permits nothing, so it does make clothing טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every invalid pinching is treated the same. An invalid pinching inside is left out, but pinching outside or pinching חולין is included.

phrases.english: It includes one who pinches
(Ketz chefetz is a memory sign)
phrases.notes: Each word's letters hint at a case: ק and ץ for קדשים outside, and the letters of חפץ for חולין inside and outside.

phrases.english: sacred birds outside,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹלֵק חוּלִּין בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: and one who pinches non-sacred birds, whether inside or outside;
since they do not permit anything forbidden,
they make clothing impure while in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 13 showed what the rule leaves out. This step shows what it includes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Pinching קדשים outside, and pinching חולין inside or outside, permits nothing forbidden. So these make clothing טמא in the throat.

steps.title: Another ברייתא about birds slaughtered in the wrong place
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא asks whether slaughtering חולין inside the עזרה, or קדשים inside or outside, makes clothing טמא in the throat. It answers no, from the word 'נבלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: You might think that slaughtering a non-sacred bird inside the עזרה, or a sacred bird inside or outside, makes clothing טמא in the throat. So the פסוק says 'נבלה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא. It deals with birds killed by שחיטה in the wrong place and says they do not make clothing טמא in the throat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא was about a bird killed by מליקה in the wrong way. This one is about שחיטה. The first source it gives is the word 'נבלה', meaning such a bird does not count as a נבלה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier ברייתא. That one was about מליקה (pinching). This one is about שחיטה (slaughtering with a knife).

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
One might think that slaughtering non-sacred birds inside,
or sacred birds, whether inside or outside,
makes clothing impure while in the throat?
Therefore the verse says: 'a carcass.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא, built like the first one, about שחיטה instead of מליקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering חולין inside the עזרה, or קדשים inside or outside, does not make clothing טמא in the throat, and the source given is 'נבלה'.

steps.title: But these birds are also a נבלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that such birds are also a נבלה, so 'נבלה' cannot be the source that leaves them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is also a נבלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source the ברייתא gave. It makes the same objection it made earlier against the first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird slaughtered in the wrong place is not properly killed, so it is a נבלה. The word 'נבלה' should therefore include it, not leave it out.

phrases.english: But this too is a carcass!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the word 'נבלה' as the source that leaves these birds out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These birds are a נבלה themselves, so the word 'נבלה' cannot leave them out.

steps.title: The source is 'טריפה': only what is the same inside and outside
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is read as learning from 'טריפה'. Just as a טריפה is the same inside the עזרה and outside, only birds that are the same inside and outside make clothing טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק says 'טריפה'. Just as a טריפה is the same inside as outside, so too everything that makes clothing טמא is the same inside as outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source, the word 'טריפה', and sets up a rule for which birds make clothing טמא in the throat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is forbidden no matter where it is slaughtered. So the rule is: a bird causes this טומאה only if its status does not change based on inside or outside the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal defect

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says: 'a tereifa';
just as a tereifa is the same inside as outside,
so too, all that are the same inside as outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by changing the source from 'נבלה' to 'טריפה'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source with a different word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא learned from the word 'נבלה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא learns from 'טריפה': only a bird whose status is the same inside and outside makes clothing טמא.

steps.title: Applying the rule: these birds are left out
steps.stepSummary: Because חולין slaughtered inside, and קדשים slaughtered inside or outside, are not the same inside as outside, they do not make clothing טמא in the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: So slaughtering חולין inside, and קדשים whether inside or outside, is left out. Since they are not the same inside as outside, they do not make clothing טמא in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies its new rule to the cases it started with and leaves them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא claims these birds are 'not the same inside as outside', so they fail the טריפה test. That is why they do not cause טומאה in the throat.

phrases.english: This leaves out slaughtering non-sacred birds inside,
and sacred birds, whether inside or outside –
since they are not the same inside as outside,
they do not make clothing impure while in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 17 to the cases of step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the ברייתא, חולין slaughtered inside and קדשים slaughtered anywhere do not make clothing טמא in the throat, because they are not the same inside as outside.

steps.title: Granted for חולין, but קדשים are invalid both inside and outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the reasoning for חולין but asks about קדשים. A sacred bird slaughtered inside or outside is invalid either way, so it seems the same inside as outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, חולין are not the same inside as outside. But קדשים are invalid in both cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reasoning for sacred birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-sacred bird slaughtered outside is permitted, but inside it is forbidden, so it really is different inside and outside. A sacred bird slaughtered by שחיטה is invalid both inside and outside. So it seems just like a טריפה and should make clothing טמא.

phrases.english: Granted, non-sacred birds –
are not the same inside as outside;
but sacred birds –
in both this case and that case they are disqualified!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא חוּלִּין לֹא שָׁווּ בִּפְנִים כְּבַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 18 applied the rule to קדשים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קדשים slaughtered inside or outside are 'not the same inside as outside'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קדשים slaughtered by שחיטה are invalid both inside and outside, so they are the same in both places. By the טריפה rule they should make clothing טמא.

steps.title: רבא: slaughter outside that brings כרת also removes נבלה status
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question about קדשים slaughtered outside with logic. If the slaughter counts enough to make the person liable for כרת, it must also count enough to keep the bird from being a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If slaughtering it outside counts enough to make him liable for כרת, will it not count enough to keep the bird from being a נבלה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 19 about sacred birds slaughtered outside the עזרה. He does not use a פסוק. He uses plain logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who slaughters a sacred animal outside the עזרה is liable for כרת, so the תורה treats that slaughter as a real שחיטה. If it is real enough for punishment, it is real enough to keep the bird from becoming a נבלה. That means it cannot make clothing טמא in the throat.

keyTerms.meaning: slaughtering a sacred animal outside the עזרה
spiritual cutting off, the punishment for slaughtering sacred animals outside
out of the status of a נבלה

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the bird is a kosher sacrifice. It is still invalid. The only point is that the slaughter counts enough that the bird is not a נבלה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If slaughter outside was effective for it
to make him liable for karet,
will it not be effective to make it pure
from the status of a nevelah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם הוֹעִילָה לוֹ שְׁחִיטַת חוּץ לְחַיְּיבוֹ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19's question about קדשים slaughtered outside, using logic instead of the 'same inside and outside' rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New logical source (קל וחומר style reasoning) replacing the verse-based reason for the outside case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sacred birds slaughtered outside seem the same inside and outside, so they should make clothing טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Slaughter outside counts enough to bring כרת, so it counts enough to keep the bird from being a נבלה.

steps.title: What about sacred birds slaughtered inside?
steps.stepSummary: רבא's logic covers slaughter outside. The גמרא asks what the source is for slaughter inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for outside. Where do we learn the case of inside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא's reason only works for slaughter outside. It is setting up the next step by asking how we know the law for a sacred bird slaughtered inside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרת that רבא relied on is the punishment for slaughtering an offering outside the עזרה. Slaughtering a sacred bird inside brings no כרת, so רבא's 'if it brings כרת' argument does not reach it. A different source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found outside;
phrases.notes: He means the case of a sacred bird slaughtered outside, which רבא just explained.

phrases.english: inside, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notices that רבא's answer covers only half the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a sacred bird slaughtered inside the עזרה does not make clothing טמא in the throat.

steps.title: Inside is not the same as outside
steps.stepSummary: Slaughter inside does not match slaughter outside, since only outside brings כרת. So the 'same inside and outside' rule leaves it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is not the same inside as outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a sacred bird slaughtered inside is left out by the rule learned from טריפה: only birds that are the same inside and outside make clothing טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 claimed sacred birds are the same inside and outside, because both are invalid. רבא's point shows a difference: slaughter outside brings כרת and slaughter inside does not. Because the two cases are not equal, the slaughter inside fails the test and does not make clothing טמא.

phrases.english: Since they are not the same
inside as outside.
phrases.notes: This is the rule learned from טריפה back in Step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21's question by bringing back the rule from Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Slaughter inside differs from slaughter outside (no כרת compared with כרת), so it is not the same inside and outside and does not make clothing טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now both cases from the ברייתא in Step 15 have a source: outside from רבא's logic, inside from the 'same inside and outside' rule.

steps.title: Then pinching sacred birds outside should also not cause impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if being different inside and outside exempts a bird, then a sacred bird pinched outside should also be exempt. Pinching is valid inside and invalid outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a sacred bird that one pinched outside should also not make clothing טמא, since pinching is not the same inside as outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule just used. It shows the rule would wrongly exempt a sacred bird pinched outside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מליקה inside the עזרה makes a valid offering, and מליקה outside makes an invalid one. So pinching is also 'not the same inside and outside.' By that rule a bird pinched outside should not make clothing טמא, yet the משנה rules that it does, because it counts as a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: he pinched (killed a bird offering by מליקה, with the כהן's thumbnail)

phrases.english: If so,
if one pinched sacred birds outside, they should also not make clothing impure,
since they are not the same inside as outside!
phrases.notes: Pinching inside makes a valid offering, while pinching outside makes it invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מָלַק קָדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'not the same inside and outside' reasoning just used in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'not the same inside and outside' to exempt sacred birds from causing טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule proves too much. It would exempt a sacred bird pinched outside, which the משנה treats as a נבלה that makes clothing טמא.

steps.title: Compare improper with improper, not improper with proper
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי explains that we may compare one improperly done act with another, but not an improper act with a proper one. Slaughter outside and slaughter inside are both improper, so we compare them. Pinching outside is improper and pinching inside is proper, so we do not compare them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: We may learn something done improperly from something else done improperly. We may not learn something done improperly from something done properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי answers the challenge by limiting when the 'same inside and outside' test is used. It applies only when both actions being compared are improper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a bird offering is improper both inside and outside, so we may compare the two. They differ, because only outside brings כרת, and so the bird does not make clothing טמא. Pinching inside is the proper way to bring the offering, so it cannot be set against pinching outside. That case keeps its normal status as a נבלה that makes clothing טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: not in its valid manner, done improperly
done in its valid manner, the proper way

steps.whatToRemember: A sacred bird slaughtered inside or outside the עזרה does not make clothing טמא in the throat. A sacred bird pinched outside does, because pinching outside cannot be compared to proper pinching inside.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets the limits of the 'same inside and outside' test. It explains why slaughter and מליקה of sacred birds lead to opposite results.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
We derive an item done not in its valid manner
from an item done not in its valid manner;
phrases.notes: Slaughter outside compared with slaughter inside: both are the wrong method for a bird offering.

phrases.english: but we do not derive an item done not in its valid manner
from an item done in its valid manner.
phrases.notes: Pinching inside is the proper way, so it cannot be compared with pinching outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בְּהֶיכְשֵׁרוֹ מִדָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בְּהֶיכְשֵׁרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves Step 23's challenge by limiting the comparison rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a comparison principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any difference between inside and outside exempts the bird, so pinching outside should be exempt too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a difference between two improper acts counts. Pinching outside cannot be compared with proper pinching inside, so it remains a נבלה.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to compare an improper offering with a proper one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שימי בר אשי's rule from a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns that a יוצא that went up on the מזבח stays there, because a יוצא is valid on a במה. That is learning an invalid case from a valid case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we really not learn an improper case from a proper one? But a ברייתא teaches: How do we know that an offering that left the עזרה, if it went up on the מזבח, does not come down? Because an offering that left is valid on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule just stated in Step 24. It brings a ברייתא that seems to do exactly what רב שימי בר אשי said we may not do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בית המקדש, an offering that went out of the עזרה (יוצא) is disqualified, so it is improper. On a private altar (במה), going out does not matter, so there it is proper. The ברייתא uses the proper במה case to teach about the improper מקדש case, which goes against Step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering that went out of the עזרה and became disqualified
If a disqualified offering went up on the מזבח, it is not taken down
A private altar, allowed in certain periods when there was no בית המקדש

phrases.english: And can we not? But isn't it taught:
phrases.notes: He means: can we really not learn an improper case from a proper one, like Step 24 said?

phrases.english: From where do we know about an offering that went out
that if it went up on the altar, it does not come down?
Since an offering that went out is valid on a private altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of רב שימי בר אשי given in Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that we may not compare an improper act with a proper act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns the law of an invalid יוצא in the מקדש from a valid יוצא on a במה, which is comparing improper with proper

steps.title: The real source is the פסוק, and the במה only gives support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's real source is 'זאת תורת העולה', which includes everything that went up on the מזבח. The במה reasoning is only extra support, not the actual source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא of that ברייתא relies on the פסוק 'This is the law of the burnt offering', which includes this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 24's rule. It says the ברייתא does not really learn the law from the במה case. It learns it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זאת תורת העולה' are read as including any disqualified item that went up on the מזבח: it stays there. Since the law comes from the פסוק, the ברייתא is not truly comparing improper with proper. So רב שימי בר אשי's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the law of the burnt offering' (ויקרא 6:2), read as including disqualified items that went up on the מזבח
Included: the פסוק adds more cases
He relies on it, meaning this is his real source

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of רב שימי בר אשי stands: we compare improper with improper, not improper with proper. The ברייתא gets its law from 'זאת תורת העולה'.

phrases.english: The teacher of that teaching, on "This is the law of the burnt offering"
which includes this case, relies.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא אַ״זֹּאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה״ רִיבָּה סְמִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the source: the law comes from a פסוק, not from comparing to a במה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא learns the law of a יוצא from the valid במה case
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא learns it from 'זאת תורת העולה', and the במה only supports it

steps.title: New משנה: a pinched bird found to be a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. If a כהן pinched a bird properly and then found it was a טריפה, רבי מאיר says it does not cause the impurity of a bird נבלה when swallowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he pinched the bird and it was found to be a טריפה, רבי מאיר says: it does not make a person impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It brings רבי מאיר's ruling about a properly pinched bird that turns out to be a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher bird that died without proper killing (נבלה) makes a person impure when he swallows an olive-sized piece. רבי מאיר holds that proper מליקה keeps the bird from being a נבלה, even though it turned out to be a טריפה. So it does not cause that impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: He pinched: the כהן killed the bird with his fingernail at the back of the neck
An animal or bird with a fatal defect
The throat; a kosher bird נבלה makes a person impure when it is swallowed

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he pinched the bird and it was found to be a tereifa,
Rabbi Meir says:
it does not make a person impure in the throat,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a properly pinched bird that is found to be a טריפה does not cause impurity in the throat
